examples.en: I pressed my clothes tightly into the bag.
You have to roll the gimbap tightly so it doesn't burst.

examples.ko: 상자 안에 책이 꽉꽉 들어차 있어요.
examples.en: The box is packed full of books.

examples.ko: 주말 아침인데 지하철이 사람으로 꽉꽉 찼어요.
examples.en: Even though it's a weekend morning, the subway was jam-packed with people.
I tie my shoelaces tight and run.
I packed the snow firmly and made a snowman.

explain: '꽉'보다 여러 번 힘을 주거나 빈틈없이 가득 채우는 느낌이 더 강해요. '꽉꽉 눌러 담다', '꽉꽉 채우다', '꽉꽉 들어차다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.

phrases.en: I packed the suitcase tight with clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빈틈이 없도록 가득 넣는다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to fill something with no gaps.

phrases.example: 지하철 안에 사람들이 꽉꽉 들어차 있어요.
phrases.en: The subway is packed full of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 빈자리 없이 가득한 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people or things filling a space with no room left.

phrases.en: Hold the handle tight so you don't fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽉꽉'은 여러 번 힘을 주지만, '꽉'은 한 번 단단히 잡거나 누를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 꽉꽉 means repeated force, while 꽉 is one firm grip or press.

explain_en: Compared with '꽉', it feels more emphatic, as if you press repeatedly or leave no gap at all. It often appears in set combinations such as '꽉꽉 눌러 담다', '꽉꽉 채우다' and '꽉꽉 들어차다'.

en: to take in; to drag in

examples.en: Why are you dragging me into this too?
I don't want to drag my friend into the quarrel.
He persuaded people and drew them into the plan.
Please don't bring unrelated people into the conversation.

examples.ko: 이 장면에 음악을 끌어넣으면 더 좋을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think it would be better to bring music into this scene.

examples.ko: 가족 문제까지 회사 일에 끌어넣으면 곤란해요.
examples.en: It's awkward if you drag even family issues into work.

explain: 원래 상관없던 사람이나 일을 어떤 상황 안으로 끌고 들어올 때 써요. '끌어들이다'와 비슷하지만 억지로 넣는다는 느낌이 있어서 '나를 끌어넣지 마세요'처럼 불만을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 저는 상관없으니까 이 일에 끌어넣지 마세요.
phrases.en: It has nothing to do with me, so please don't drag me into this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원치 않는 일에 엮이고 싶지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you don't want to be involved in something.

phrases.en: I brought my friend into the business.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끌어넣다'보다 억지로 넣는 느낌이 덜하고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less forceful than '끌어넣다' and used more often.

phrases.example: 아이들을 어른들의 싸움에 끌어넣으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't drag children into adults' fights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 상관없던 사람을 갈등에 엮을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pulling someone unrelated into a conflict.

explain_en: It is used when pulling a person or matter into a situation they had nothing to do with. It is similar to '끌어들이다' but feels more forced, so it often appears in complaints like '나를 끌어넣지 마세요'.

examples.en: This meeting opened the way for dialogue.
Water trickles out of the paddy's water outlet.
That one remark became the start of the negotiation.

examples.ko: 화해의 물꼬를 트기 위해 먼저 연락해 봤어요.
examples.en: I contacted them first to break the ice and start making up.

examples.ko: 대화의 물꼬만 트이면 문제는 쉽게 풀려요.
examples.en: Once the conversation gets started, the problem is easily solved.
The water outlet in the paddy ridge broke and the water overflowed.

explain: 원래는 논에 물이 드나들게 만든 작은 통로인데, 요즘은 뉴스나 일상에서 '물꼬를 트다' 꼴로 훨씬 자주 써요. 일이나 대화가 막힌 데서 처음 풀리기 시작하는 계기를 말해요. 보통 '대화', '협상', '화해', '교류' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: The two companies opened the way for cooperation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막혀 있던 일이나 관계가 풀리기 시작하는 계기를 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means creating the first opening that lets a stuck matter or relationship begin to move.
phrases.en_equiv: break the ice; open the way

explain_en: It originally means a small passage that lets water in and out of a rice paddy, but today it is far more often used in the form '물꼬를 트다'. It refers to the first step that starts to unblock a stuck matter. It usually appears with words like dialogue, negotiation, reconciliation and exchange.

examples.en: I went around every weekend looking for a new home.

examples.ko: 회사에서 새 사무실 자리를 물색하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is searching for a spot for a new office.

examples.ko: 친구에게 줄 선물을 물색해 봤지만 마땅한 게 없어요.
examples.en: I looked around for a gift for my friend, but found nothing suitable.

examples.ko: 신혼집을 물색할 때는 교통을 가장 먼저 봐요.
examples.en: When looking for a newlywed home, I check transportation first.

examples.ko: 감독이 새 주인공을 물색한다는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that the director is searching for a new lead.

examples.ko: 마음에 드는 가게를 물색했는데 값이 비쌌어요.
examples.en: I found a shop I liked after searching, but it was expensive.

explain: 조건에 맞는 것을 이리저리 알아보며 고른다는 느낌이에요. 집, 장소, 사람, 선물에 쓰고, 잃어버린 물건을 찾을 때는 '찾다'를 써요. 말보다는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 새 직원을 물색 중이에요.
phrases.en: Our company is looking for a new employee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 알아보고 고르는 중이라는 진행의 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you are in the middle of searching and choosing.

phrases.example: 모임 장소를 물색해서 다음 주에 알려 드릴게요.
phrases.en: I'll look for a place for the meeting and let you know next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건에 맞는 장소를 이리저리 고를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for picking a place that fits certain conditions.

phrases.en: I'm looking into houses to move to on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물색하다'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 바꿔 말할 수 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday replacement for 물색하다 in conversation.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of looking around and choosing something that fits your conditions. It is used for homes, places, people and gifts, but for lost items you use '찾다'. It appears more in writing and the news than in speech.

examples.en: I think the customer groups need to be broken down further.
Market segmentation is the basis of marketing.
Thanks to the division of tasks into smaller parts, work got faster.
If the subdivision goes too far, things actually get complicated.
Jobs are becoming more and more specialized.
The students asked for the lesson content to be broken into finer parts.

explain: 하나를 여러 작은 부분으로 나눈다는 뜻이라서 시장, 업무, 직업, 등급처럼 큰 덩어리가 대상일 때 잘 써요. '세분화가 되다'보다 '세분화가 필요하다', '세분화가 진행되다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Jobs are becoming more and more subdivided.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 더 잘게 나뉘는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change in which things get divided more finely on their own.

phrases.en: If you divide the work into small parts, it gets easier.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, everyday way to say what 세분화 means.

phrases.en: I am working on subdividing the data.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나누는 일 자체를 하나의 작업으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the act of dividing is treated as a task in itself.

explain_en: It means splitting one big thing into many smaller parts, so it suits targets like markets, tasks, jobs and grades. People more often say '세분화가 필요하다' or '세분화가 진행되다' than '세분화가 되다'.

examples.ko: 시간 안배를 잘 못해서 시험 문제를 다 못 풀었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't manage my time well, so I couldn't finish all the exam questions.

examples.ko: 힘 안배를 잘해야 마라톤을 끝까지 달릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pace your energy well to run the whole marathon.

examples.ko: 자리 안배에 신경 써서 손님들을 앉혔어요.
examples.en: I took care with the seating arrangement when seating the guests.

examples.ko: 인원 안배가 맞지 않아서 팀을 다시 나눴어요.
examples.en: The distribution of people wasn't balanced, so we split the teams again.
The budget was allocated in a balanced way.

examples.ko: 공정한 안배를 위해 지역별로 위원을 뽑았어요.
examples.en: For fair distribution, they chose committee members by region.

explain: '시간 안배', '힘 안배', '자리 안배'처럼 앞에 무엇을 나눌지 붙여서 써요. 형편을 고려해서 알맞게 나누어 두는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '조절하다', '나눠서 쓰다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 시간 안배를 잘하면 숙제가 빨리 끝나요.
phrases.en: If you divide your time well, homework gets done quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 나누어 쓰는 계획을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for planning how to divide time.

phrases.en: I couldn't pace my strength, so I got tired at the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체력을 나누어 쓰는 일을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: That player paces well in a match.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안배'에 '잘하다'를 붙여 잘 나누어 쓴다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'jalhada' means one distributes things well.

explain_en: It is used with the thing being divided in front, as in '시간 안배', '힘 안배' and '자리 안배'. It suggests dividing things appropriately, taking the situation into account. In everyday talk people also say '조절하다' or '나눠서 쓰다'.
